description: Recommends new transit bylaw with fines, bans, fare enforcement.
Amends public spitting and appeal board bylaws.

chips.text: Recommended
Mayor Block moved to maintain prior pet policy, requiring kennels or service animals.
Families with children under six affected by supervision requirement.
Administration sought relaxed pet rules to reduce operator conflict
Who decides what a service animal is, and is it regulated?
Bus Riders of Saskatoon supported safety intent but questioned pet rules and child supervision.
Sporadic enforcement could lead to harassment and discrimination charges.
Concerns raised about collecting fines from homeless individuals.
Bylaws to be drafted for July Council, effective September 1, 2026.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: New Transit Bylaw
said: Supports bylaw's goal to enhance transit safety and order.
Questions relaxed pet policy and child supervision age (under 16).
Recommends public engagement on bylaw details and enforcement.

description: Saskatoon Transit will implement a policing program and new bylaw.
New bylaw allows officers to issue tickets for fare evasion.
Education campaign and smart card system will improve compliance.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Councillor Pearce questioned the accuracy of the 1.8% fare evasion rate.
High school students are identified as a group with high fare evasion.
Council inquired about dedicated buses for unhoused; staff cited feasibility and resource concerns.
The true extent of fare evasion beyond the reported 1.8% remains unknown.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon advocated for affordable mobility for homeless riders.
Concerns raised about the impact of enforcement on unhoused individuals unable to pay fares.
Administration will provide a full update on the transit policing program in Q4 this year.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Saskatoon Transit Fare Evasion Update
said: Recorded fare evasion is likely higher than reported 1.8%.
Enforcement costs may exceed lost fares; not all evaders would pay.
Address poverty-related evasion with affordable options, not fines.

description: Saskatoon Transit redesigns bus network for June 2026 launch.
Public engagement continues through Fall 2026 and Spring 2027.
Project has $100,000 budget over three years.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer questioned survey wording on distance and directness, suggesting potential skew.
Councillor asked how much of the $100,000 budget has been spent to date.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon advocated for more hands-on and in-depth engagement for transit users.
Dedicated engagement sessions were held with newcomers in the first phase.
Administration stated the $100,000 budget should cover all project phases.

speakers.name: Peter Gallen
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Saskatoon Transit Bus Network Redesign Update
said: Advocates for better, more hands-on engagement in phase two.
Stresses critical need for riders to provide specific feedback.
Calls for deeper, iterative engagement with knowledgeable stakeholders.

description: Saskatoon Transit expanded service to Brighton, Rosewood, and Aspen Ridge.
Ridership decreased 6.7% in 2025, but peak routes remain full.
City plans $23.5 million for new buses and improved Access Transit.

chips.text: City Manager explained Saskatchewan's unique untethered provincial revenue sharing model.
International students may be affected by ridership changes due to enrollment shifts.
Is 1% provincial transit funding average across Canada?
Access Transit denial rate reduced from 9.9% to 9%.
Staff committed to providing updates on summer and fall route adjustments.
